prompt: Five keypad buttons share one ActionListener. Complete actionPerformed so it routes on e.getActionCommand(): digits append to the display (max six), CLR clears it, OK captures and clears it.
explanation: Every ActionEvent carries an action command string, which for a button defaults to its text, so one listener can serve a whole keypad without keeping references to the individual buttons. Switching on that string keeps the routing in one readable place, and a default branch handles "anything else", here the digits. The length guard shows why the handler must inspect current state before changing it.
hints: String works in a switch statement: switch (e.getActionCommand()) { case "CLR": ... }.
Use the default branch for the digits so adding a fourth digit button needs no new code.
Before appending, check display.getText().length() so the display never grows past six characters.
